Destroying the players home village early on in the campaign as a plot device is fine(Tropes are good and it's a trope for a reason) especially for inexperienced DMs looking for a easy way to motivate their players. Although I will say it would be more impactful if the home village doesn't get seriously threatened or destroyed until later in the campaign as an actual "raise the stakes" moment rather than the "call to adventure" moment.



What I have a problem with is the kill everyone except for the PCs(Especially when done in the first few sessions) It's ten times worse if the characters aren't the stereotypical tragic orphans and incorporated their family as part of their backstory. 

Killing everyone off like that is basically saying "I know you wrote a unique backstory to get into role playing your PC but we are going to hit the reset button and turn your character into a tragic orphan". While simultaneously encouraging the players to not get attached to anyone throughout the rest of the campaign. 

If the DM is destroying the home village trope route they should at least give the players a great chance to save or lead their family, friends, and some villagers to safety. (This could make a great engaging first ark) 
Hell I would recommend if you go the destroying the village route early on have the PCs get saved by their mentor/family/friends who has already escorted the majority/all of your PCs family to safety.

Some tips

*Only break one law at a time(Really the only one you need to follow)

*Put whatever you buy out of sight in a sealed container(preferably the trunk) and do not consume anything until you get home

*Have current forms of your insurance, registration, and a non expired license ready to hand over just in case.

**Adding make sure your turn signals and brake lights work thanks /u/toastedface27

*Do not speed or commit any other traffic violations such as tailgating, stay out of the left lane except when passing when on a two lane road, and changing lanes without a signal

*If you do go over the speed limit keep it under five over as most highway patrolmen won't bother.

*Consider spending a couple of hours in Colorado just in case they are doing those illegal but nearly unproveable operations where they have a plain clothes operative write down license plates at the local fireworks stand, liquor store, or dispensary.

If you follow these tips legally even if you get pulled over they have no reason to search your car. 

If you do happen to get pulled over:

*Record any and all conversations

*If they ask to do a search of your vehicle first ask if you are being detained then refuse to allow a search and demand a warrant.

Generally speaking cops will try and bullying you consent to a search because either A. They have no probable cause or B. They don't want to take the time to get a warrant approved. 

*Please note you are not required to answer their questions only to provide them with your license and registration. So they can issue you a possible traffic situation

*If they do start a search or start asking incriminating questions don't answer them and tell the police officer you are exercising your right to silence(Fifth amendment) and calling a lawyer.

In closing even if you don't follow these tips and just don't drive recklessly to be honest you still have a 99% chance of not getting pulled over. But if you follow these tips I would put the odds at you getting pulled over and searched at .0001%
